about.text: Chal, also shubat or khoormog, is a Turkic and Mongolic beverage of fermented camel milk, sparkling white with a sour flavor, popular in Central Asia — particularly in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. In Kazakhstan the drink is known as shubat, and is a staple summer food. Due to preparation requirements and perishable nature, chal has proved difficult to export. Agaran is collected from the surface of chal.

how.text: Kazakh shubat is camel milk backslopped with old shubat. Lactobacilli such as L. helveticus make the acid, and yeasts, chiefly lactose-fermenting K. marxianus, add a little alcohol.

processing.text: Modern shubat is made from pasteurised milk at 20–25 °C, 3–4 h plus 10–20 h; it keeps 5–6 d at 5–10 °C.
